Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for India's batting effort. The two umpires and players are out in the middle. It will be Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rohit Sharma to open the innings for India. Tim Southee will start with the new ball for New Zealand. Away we go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Right then, India will be happy to have kept New Zealand under 300, having lost the toss. Their openers have a tricky phase to negotiate before the close of play and they would ideally want to see off the phase without any casualty. With about 40 minutes of play left, it looks very likely that we'll surpass 90 overs today, even without the extra half-hour extension, which is quite rare to see. As for New Zealand, their aim will be to make the new ball count and finish the day on a high. Back in a bit for India's reply.

Washington Sundar has helped India script a remarkable turnaround. He leads the Indian team off the field. New Zealand will be disappointed to have ended up with only 259 on the board, considering the start they had. From 197/3, they lost their next 7 wickets for just 62 runs. Sundar was the star of the show, finishing with career-best figures of 7/59 in 23.1 overs. New Zealand started off well before Ravichandran Ashwin sent back the New Zealand skipper. Devon Convoy batted brilliantly along with Rachin Ravindra, the centurion from the previous Test, who both went on to score their respective fifties. Just as the Indian shoulders began to droop, Sundar dismissed Rachin and Tom Blundell in quick succession before Tea and kept chipping away at the wickets throughout the final session.

With five wickets down, the game is finely poised. India will look to capitalize on the shift in momentum as they head into the final session of the day while New Zealand will look to rebuild their innings after these twin blows. Stay tuned as we are back in a bit!

Just when it looked like New Zealand were firmly in control, Washington Sundar made a crucial breakthrough. Brought back into the attack with only three overs left before Tea, Sundar produced a stunning spell. He first removed Ravindra with a beauty and then, with the last ball before the interval, sent Tom Blundell back to the pavilion. Sundar's two quick wickets have given India some much-needed momentum heading into the break, halting New Zealand's charge.

The second session is often regarded as the best time to bat in India, with the ball typically coming onto the bat more easily. However, given the signs of turn and grip that India's spinners started to extract towards the end of the first session, batting might not be as straightforward as usual. The Kiwi batters will need to be decisive and proactive in handling India's three-pronged spin attack. Join us back at 6.40 am GMT for the start of what promises to be an intriguing second session. In the meantime, you can switch tabs and follow the action from the third Test between Pakistan and England in Rawalpindi.

India couldn’t capitalize on that breakthrough immediately, as Devon Conway and Will Young weathered the challenge posed by spin from both ends. Young couldn’t see the session through as India successfully overturned an on-field decision for a caught-behind off Ashwin’s bowling. This breakthrough brought Rachin Ravindra, the centurion from the last game, to the crease. With little assistance for the seamers, the two Kiwi openers were largely untroubled, apart from a couple of testing deliveries that caused Devon Conway some discomfort. Commentary.Commentary: All set for the action to get underway in Pune. A good crowd is in on a hazy Thursday morning and should build as the day progresses. Rohit Sharma leads his troops out to the centre. They are joined by the two Kiwi openers, Tom Latham and Devon Conway. Jasprit Bumrah has the new ball in hand and he is raring to go. Three slips and a gully in place. Here we go!

The captain of India, Rohit Sharma says that they would have batted first as well. Adds that regardless of the pitch, they need to play good cricket. Shares that there were a lot of positives in the last game. Feels that no matter what the situation is, it is important how you find your way back into the game and he is happy that they did that in Bengaluru. Mentions that not having enough runs on the board hurt them in the previous game. Reckons that this wicket looks a little drier and they will try to make the most of whatever moisture is available early on. Informs that they have made three changes with Shubman Gill, Akash Deep and Washington Sundar coming in for KL Rahul, Mohammed Siraj and Kuldeep Yadav.

Tom Latham, the New Zealand captain, chooses to bat first, noting the pitch looks different from Bengaluru but hopes to set a solid total. He observes that there's not much grass on the surface, which is expected in this part of the world, and predicts it might spin later in the game. Latham expresses pride in his team’s effort, especially after last week's win, and emphasises the importance of adapting quickly to the surface. He mentions the importance of carrying forward the confidence from the previous match and confirms one change - Matt Henry misses out due to a glute niggle and Mitchell Santner comes in for him.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Tom Latham (C), Devon Conway, Will Young, Rachin Ravindra, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Blundell (WK), Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner (In for Matt Henry), Tim Southee, Ajaz Patel, William O'Rourke.

India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma (C), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shubman Gill (In for KL Rahul), Virat Kohli, Rishabh Pant (WK), Sarfaraz Khan, Ravindra Jadeja, Ravichandran Ashwin, Washington Sundar (In for Kuldeep Yadav), Jasprit Bumrah, Akash Deep (In for Mohammed Siraj).
TOSS - New Zealand have won the toss and they will BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Simon Doull is near the deck. He informs that rain has been around in Pune and therefore, the outfield is a bit damp but we should be fine to start on time. Dinesh Karthik joins him and says that the colour of the pitch remains the same as Bengaluru since both are black soil surfaces. Adds that here in Pune, the soil has been locally resourced, resulting in more moisture retention. Karthik notes that the good-length areas are a lot dry and devoid of grass. Opines that the team winning the toss should look to bat first.

The excitement is building for what promises to be a thrilling encounter. India will be desperate to elevate their game and bounce back, while New Zealand will be eager to seal the series and make history. Who will come out on top? Stay tuned for an intense battle ahead. Toss and team news coming up shortly!

For New Zealand, their win in Bengaluru was a testament to their resilience and adaptability. Their pacers exploited the conditions perfectly, dismantling India for just 46 runs in the first innings. Though India mounted a strong fightback in the second innings, New Zealand’s composed batting, especially from Rachin Ravindra, ensured a comfortable win. Captain Tom Latham now leads his side into a different challenge - a turning track in Pune, where spin will likely dominate. With Kane Williamson still unavailable due to his ongoing rehabilitation from a groin strain, Latham will need to lead by example. Much will depend on how they handle this 'turning test', and the toss could play a vital role in shaping the game.

The conditions in Pune will be familiar for the Indian side, with the slow, turning track expected to aid their formidable spin attack. Key players like Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma will be eyeing big scores, especially after both struggled to convert starts into centuries in their last outing. With the pressure mounting, the stage is perfectly set for them to come to the party. One of the key discussion points for India will be their team selection. After KL Rahul’s struggles in the first Test and Sarfaraz Khan’s impressive 150, Rahul’s place in the XI is under scrutiny. There are strong indications from head coach Gautam Gambhir that Shubman Gill, now fully fit, could return to the playing XI.

Hello and welcome from Pune for the start of the much-anticipated second Test between India and New Zealand! In the series opener in Bengaluru, both teams traded blows, but it was New Zealand who landed the crucial first strike and followed it up with the knockout punch to take the lead in the series. India, however, will be eager to make amends and level the series, while the Kiwis have a shot at creating history - doing what no team has managed in over a decade - beating India in a Test series on their home soil.
